name: bash
description: Run a shell command in the project folder. Returns stdout, stderr and exit code.

name: read_file
description: Read a text file (project folder or skill folder). Optional offset/limit in lines.

name: write_file
description: Write a text file inside the project folder (creates folders, overwrites).

name: list_dir
description: List a directory (project or skill folder).

name: ask_user
description: Ask the user 1 to 4 multiple-choice questions, shown as cards. Recommended option first. Returns the answers.

name: show_page
description: Open an HTML file in the preview pane (project or skill folder).

name: screenshot_preview
description: Take a screenshot of what the preview pane shows now and get it back as an image, to look at a contact sheet, a card page or a reel. Open the page with show_page first. Optional javascript runs in the page before the capture: to look at a reel at t seconds, set the seek slider, for example document.getElementById('seek').value = t*10; document.getElementById('seek').dispatchEvent(new Event('input')). Only describe what you actually see.

javascript.description: optional script run in the page before the capture

wait_ms.description: wait before the capture, default 600, max 5000

name: get_state
description: Read the project's state: showreel.json (parameters, decisions including the look, gates, step, scenes), the assets (id, type, status, scenes, note), the blocks of the sidebar with their status, the block and file the user has in front of them, and the top-level files. Call it before you propose anything, so you do not ask what the app already holds.

name: propose_edit
description: Offer a change to a project file the app does not model (replaces its whole content). The user sees a diff and accepts or refuses; nothing is written before that, unless they switched on apply-directly for the project. Use it for storyboard.md until the storyboard block exists, and for text files. Not for showreel.json or assets/MANIFEST.csv (use update_parameter and update_asset: they refuse file writes). brief.md, style-sheet.md and storyboard.md are generated from showreel.json: a change to one is offered back to the user as a re-import. If the answer says the file changed since, read it again and propose a new edit. Creating a new file and writing code can use write_file.

content.description: the complete new content of the file

note.description: one short line saying what changes and why, shown above the diff

name: update_parameter
description: Change one field of the Project block. The user sees a plain card (before and after) and accepts or refuses; nothing changes before that, unless they switched on apply-directly. Keys: name, audience, message, tone, constraints (free text), conversationLanguage (code), reelLanguages and formats (comma-separated), duration (seconds). An empty value clears the field.

name: update_asset
description: Change one asset of the Resources block by its id (from get_state): status (proposed, approved, excluded, placeholder, hold; a hold needs a note), note, licence_note, or the scenes that use it (for example S01,S07). The user sees a plain card and accepts or refuses. Approving a file held for confidential data or a forbidden font licence is refused: that goes through the skill's organiser.

name: open_block
description: Switch the user's window to a block of the sidebar: project, look, resources, storyboard, scene, build or deliver. Blocks that are not built yet answer so: say it and carry on in the chat.

name: update_decision
description: Change one decision of the Look block. The user sees a plain card (before and after) and accepts or refuses; nothing changes before that, unless they switched on apply-directly. Keys: palette (colours as #RRGGBB, comma-separated, in the order background, text, accent, accent 2; at most 6), titleFont and textFont (a font name; prefer the free list of the skill, a font that is not in it is flagged for its licence), background (an id of the engine's backgrounds), backgroundMood (punch, playful, tech, clean, cinematic or deadpan: how an animated background reacts to music), moods (one or two mood packs of the effects catalogue, comma-separated) and effectsPack (one pack). An empty value clears the decision. Unknown ids are refused with the list of valid ones.

name: add_scene
description: Add a scene to the storyboard, with the next free ID (or the ID you give, S04b style, if it is free). Propose one scene per call, in order, with a start and an end and a line short enough for the reading budget (about 3 s for a line of six to eight words). The user sees a plain card (before and after) and accepts or refuses; nothing changes before that, unless they switched on apply-directly. Scene IDs are stable: never reused, never renumbered, a ditched scene stays in the list marked ditched. Changing the text, timing or look of a scene the user already marked OK sends it back to review, and after the Go it takes the Go back (the card says so): that is the user's rule, not yours to work around. You can never give the Go; only the user can, with the Go button.

end.description: end time in seconds, after the start

handoff.description: what hands over to the next scene

in_cuts.description: the cut-downs this scene belongs to, for example 15s, 45s

status.description: only the user decides OK in the app; ditched keeps the ID marked

assets.description: ids of the linked assets (from get_state), comma-separated: replaces the links of this scene

after.description: position: put the scene after this scene ID, or 'start'. A move never changes an ID.

name: update_scene
description: Change one scene by its ID (from get_state): times, text, image and motion, feeling, handoff, cuts, note, status, linked assets, or position. The user sees a plain card (before and after) and accepts or refuses; nothing changes before that, unless they switched on apply-directly. Scene IDs are stable: never reused, never renumbered, a ditched scene stays in the list marked ditched. Changing the text, timing or look of a scene the user already marked OK sends it back to review, and after the Go it takes the Go back (the card says so): that is the user's rule, not yours to work around. You can never give the Go; only the user can, with the Go button.

handoff.description: what hands over to the next scene

in_cuts.description: the cut-downs this scene belongs to, for example 15s, 45s

status.description: only the user decides OK in the app; ditched keeps the ID marked

assets.description: ids of the linked assets (from get_state), comma-separated: replaces the links of this scene
